messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 [ALERT] p99 streaming stalls > SLO on prod-us-east-1 (service: decode-inference). Started 1911122334. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.
maya: I see the alert, pulling traces. p95 also creeping up.
devon: any deploys in last hour?
aj: yes, pushed new TRT/FlashAttention kernels + compiler flag --fast-decode at 1911121000.
maya: that matches the window. traces show heavy tail at decode stage, lots of paging/vmem spikes in logs.
samira: tagging customers with streaming sessions > 5s tokens, looks like 3 paying customers affected (CS notified).
leo: rollout was staged to 20% canary, but routing stayed at canary for specific capacity groups. This might've hit a particular hostpool.
devon: stack traces point to increased kernel compilepath misses and fallback to slow path. snippet from host /var/log/runtime: ```
[ERR] kernel_select: no optimized kernel for seq_len=2048, arch=ampere, falling back to generic kernel
[WARN] kv_cache: page-in 1.2s
```
maya: ok immediate mitigations: 1) rollback compiler flag on canary hosts 2) route new traffic to older model variant (quantized) 3) scale up dedicated pool 4) page out canary pool for deeper profiling.
aj: preparing rollback command. will run on canary hosts first. 
aj: running: `redwood-deploy rollback --service decode-inference --tag canary-trt-2026-03 --reason "rollback fast-decode flag"`
leo: re-routing 50% canary traffic to variant:v1-quant now. updating routing policy.
samira: CS pinged customers with note: "We're aware of streaming stalls, routing to alternate instance, may see transient reconnects."
devon: metrics: p99 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.1s after re-route (monitoring: https://pm.redwood/p/dash/decode). p95 trending down too.
maya: good. leave rollback running for 15m and watch for regressions. start root cause triage: is it FlashAttention change or the compiler flag?
aj: new flag toggles aggressive kernel fusion optimizations. early perf tests looked fine but didn't exercise long streaming sequences.
leo: interestingly, affected hosts had mixed driver versions (520.x) while others on 525.x. kernel selection might degrade on older drivers.
devon: can we repro on staging with same driver + long seq workload? I'll spin a job.
maya: start a repro with seq_len=2048 streaming and KV cache size ~6GB. include both latest TRT/FlashAttention and previous.
devon: repro triggered, reproduces tail stalls on driver 520 + new kernels. capturing perf counters.
samira: opening a customer impact ticket and tracking CS responses. ticket id: CS-3482.
aj: filing a bug with TRT kernel team, attaching logs and perf counters. linking compile flags and driver matrix.
leo: action items before handoff: - keep rollback on canary for 30m - run full fleet health check - schedule a hotfix build with fallback path (disable fusion) - create canary with driver=525.x to validate compatibility
maya: oncall handoff to night shift in 40m. I'll summarize for next oncall.
sre-bot: :pager: oncall-handoff scheduled to @oncall-night at 1911122410
maya: Summary for handoff: incident started 1911122334, root cause likely interaction between new TRT/FlashAttention fusion flag and older GPU driver (520.x) causing kernel selection fallback and paging -> tail latency. Mitigations: rollback flag on canary, route traffic to v1-quant, scale up pool. Next steps: repro on staging, coordinate with TRT/kernel team for hotfix, check fleet driver versions and consider constrained rollout. CS aware (CS-3482).
aj: I'll remain looped for the hotfix build. tagging @trt-kernel-team.
samira: CS will follow up with impacted customers with ETA for resolution.
leo: ok handing off to @oncall-night. please keep paging thresholds and escalation path.
maya: thanks team. I'll update thread if anything changes. :thumbsup:
